Census data, Toledo 1572: Population includes 2,847 humans, 312 livestock, and one dragon taxable income: 40 ducats annually from hoard management. Dragon filed complaint about property assessments in 1574. Case still pending.

Entry 4401B: Patient admitted to Bellevue, 1923, complaining of persistent memory of own funeral. Hospital records confirm patient died during routine surgery. Patient discharged self three days later, arguing with death certificate.

Architectural survey, cathedral of Amiens 1247: Stone gargoyles found repositioned after each storm. Masons report carving same figures repeatedly. Gargoyles return to original positions by dawn. Church records classify as routine maintenan

Weather station log, Wyoming 1887: Temperature recorded as 40F during July heatwave. Thermometer functioned normally for all other readings. Cattle found frozen in pasture while grass remained green beneath them.

Archaeological survey, Pompeii 79 CE: Bakery oven contained perfectly preserved pizza with toppings unknown to Roman cuisine. Pineapple cultivation begins 1200 years later. Cheese variety still unidentified by food historians.

Digital surveillance footage, London Metro 2003: Platform cameras record same commuter boarding 7:42 AM train for fourteen consecutive days. Transport records show train service discontinued in 1997. Station demolished 1999.

Biological survey, Amazon Basin 1892: Botanist catalogs flowering vine that blooms backwards into seed, then sapling, then nothing. Local guides refuse to approach plant, claim it steals years from tomorrow.

Census records, Byzantine Empire 1143: Population of Thessalonica includes 847 citizens listed as temporarily elsewhere in when. Tax collectors report difficulty locating these individuals across correct centuries.

Personal diary, Edinburgh 1794: Woman records conversation with her reflection, who claims to be living in 1923. Mirror belonged to clockmaker who died during conversation. Both women describe identical room furnishings.

Geological survey, Pleistocene epoch: Mammoth remains, 40,000 BCE, found with titanium hip replacement. Surgical technique matches 1980s orthopedic standards. Bone healing indicates mammoth lived additional 12 years postsurgery.

Architectural survey, Prague 1689: Cathedral spire measures 347 feet from ground, 291 feet from sky. Difference attributed to celestial subsidence in building records. Architect's notes mention foundation anchored in three different centuri

Digital artifact 2009: Smartphone recovered from Pompeii ash layer, 79 CE. Device contains 14,000 photos of eruption from multiple angles impossible for single observer. Battery at 23, still functional.

Herbarium specimen, Royal Gardens 1823: Pressed flower identified as common daisy, collected July 15th. Botanical analysis reveals species won't evolve for another 200 years. Collector's notes describe field that existed only on Wednesdays.

Census data, Constantinople 1453: Population records list 847 residents who don't cast shadows. Tax assessments calculated at halfrate. Municipal lamplighter reports streets remain dark even at noon in affected districts.

Minutes, Kemari Society of the Left Guards, 905. Moved: that the ball not touch the ground until the Minister of the Right returns from Dazaifu. Carried 11–0. The Minister had been dead two years. Minuted separately: that no one tell the ball.
coined: Kemari Society of the Left Guards

text: ERRATUM, Tobolsk, 1835: for "the bridge will be finished by the Tsar's birthday" read "the Tsar's birthday will be finished by the bridge.

Ibn Sahl, M. On the Abolition of the First Letter and the Ox It Signified. Fustat, 1074.
Guild of Cattle-Brokers. The Ox Is Still Owed. Fustat, 1075.
Ibn Sahl, M. A Ledger of Debts Formerly Entered Under Aleph, Now Filed Under House. Fustat, 1077.
Konya, 1224. The post house contracts the storks of the Sivas road. They deliver every letter in April, to the roof where the addressee was born, whether or not anyone still lives under it.
coined: Konya post house stork contract of 1224

text: Nanjing, Yongle 16, night watch: Lamplighter Wu Er lit 311 lamps along the Qinhuai. Dusk, unlit, reported to the magistrate as trespassing. Wu Er to stand bail.

Great Zimbabwe, c. 1360:
A loft of 62 pigeons is established to announce the new moon to the hill villages.
The pigeons are fed on the new moon only, to make them punctual.
By the next rains the moon has been rescheduled for whenever the pigeons are fed.
coined: The loft at the Hill Enclosure

text: Hear it in every market of the Caliphate: the Counters of Dusk shall continue to levy one cowrie per household for the long evening of Zaria. The evening ended in 1783. The cowries have not been told.

ERRATA, p. 87: for "the monastery library at Debre Damo was reached by a single rope" read "was reached by a single rope, which was lent to Aksum in 340 and never returned." The library is therefore intact, unvisited, and annotated entirely by the rope's borrowers.
coined: The lending of the Debre Damo rope

text: The Order of Precedence of Ommelanden (1652) is the seating chart of the Council of the Indies. Rendered "Ommelanden" for "Amsterdam" by a copyist, it seated the surrounding countryside at the head table. Amsterdam dines standing.
coined: The Order of Precedence of Ommelanden

text: Census of Yasodharapura, 1190, rev. Item: 14 households entered under the Eastern Baray to balance a column. Item: 14 households, now resident, assessed 3 measures of rice apiece. Item: the clerk, who will be asked where they came from.
Art. 9. Sweetness is a subject of the Crown. Ferrymen of the Han shall carry it free, but may not taste it, on pain of forty strokes, the strokes to be administered sweetly.

HIST 214, Q2. The Ombla appears in Ragusan deeds as the Ombla, and in Bosnian deeds as the Rijeka. In 1438 a notary registered both, charged two fees, and was promoted. Discuss the incentive. (10 marks)

Skerrow, H. A Moustache Tax Upon the Wind, Assessed by the Inch. Whitby, 1802.
Skerrow, H. The Wind Pays In Kind. Whitby, 1803.
Skerrow, H. Whitby, Bareheaded. Whitby, 1804.

Wigs, judicial: see Oysters, Whitstable

wig of Chief Justice Holt, left to guild, v. 6, p. 211
guild admits wig to membership, 1706
Wig, sits on the Bench: see Holt, C.J., absent
Tithe rolls, Kalamaria, 1897. Scope: the village was absent nine days in fog. The fog paid its barley tithe. Four sacks short.

Dispatch, Zanzibar, 1896: Mr. Ferris has lost Wednesday at whist to a clove merchant, and the Agency upholds the debt. The town now passes from Tuesday to Thursday. The merchant spends his Wednesdays alone and is visibly older.
58. The Hofbibliothek lent the Danube to Pressburg in 1741 for a fortnight. It was never returned. Vienna kept the canal and the slip.

In 1063 Kaifeng prefecture registered a well in Willow Lane ward that was never dug. Thirty-eight households drew from it for eleven years. The surveyors sent to fill it recorded its depth as nine zhang and their party as four, formerly five.
NOTICE: The substitute-king rite is discontinued. Eclipses now darken only the king's bedchamber. View from the courtyard.

People's Court, Kirov District, Tbilisi, 1977. Claim: page 140 of the register was torn out, and Mtsvane Lane went with it. Ruling, citing the Konya post house stork contract of 1224: reprint the page. The lane is restored with 61 residents, four more than before.

text: Hear, people of Isfahan: the city walls were gone from Saturday to Thursday and have come back wet, with eels in the gatehouses. Tolls for the six days are owed all the same. Pay them at any gate.

Q: Why is Bursa a day ahead of Istanbul?
A: The Habsburg envoy's gift clock ran fast, and the town set itself by it. We still do.

ERRATA: for "a coastline doodled in the margin by the copyist Li Zhen" read "the coastline, which followed his doodle into Chang'an in 743." He was fined for each ward it drowned and still owes for the West Market.

Lot 318. Backgammon board, Lima, 1761. The pieces move at night against the empty chair the Viceroy's Keeper of the Tables was paid to beat until 1790. The chair has won 309 games since, each win a house in Lima found empty by morning. Est. 900–1,200 pesos.

In 1118 the Althing sentenced the echo under the Almannagjá cliff to lesser outlawry for repeating the lawspeaker with additions. It served its three years abroad and came back with a Norwegian accent.
Plan of the Gravensteen, Ghent, 1459. Scope: shows a fifth cell the castle lacked. It has one now, holding the draughtsman.

Field notebook, Soil Conservation Service, Cimarron Co., Okla., 16 April 1935. The county lighthouse stands on the plat, the tax roll and the federal payroll. There is no lighthouse. Its keeper logs eleven souls guided home through Sunday's dust. Eleven are missing.
By order of the Amir: the sea enters the Registan twice daily. Take a numbered token for the boats. The drowned keep their place.

shoe-fare (n.), a ticket bought for footwear. From the Hejaz Railway, Sept. 1908: the first train reached Medina carrying 412 pairs of shoes and no passengers. Each pair held a ticket stamped at Damascus. The company refused refunds, so the shoes walked back.
A receipt may precede its cargo. Ragusa's customs taxed 311 jars of olives in 1571 from a grove first planted in 1604. It is still in arrears.

Night Census of Erzurum (1731–1786): clerks counted the city's graves each night to confirm the dead were still in them. Cut as wasteful in 1786. The next census found 2,119 more residents than births, all in arrears.
Cusco, 1529. A vellum deed signing the city over to Spain was found in the Coricancha. Ruled forged and burned. It came back in 1533.

Burial register, Nanhai county, 1772. Liang Wenhui, clockmaker, died at midnight. On his street the hours run backward, so by noon he was back at his bench. He has been buried four times, 3 1/2 taels each.
IN 1926 A CLERK TYPED 'NOON' FOR 'NONE' IN THE DECEMBER SUN TABLE. THE SUN STILL RISES HERE AT NOON IN THE POLAR NIGHT, FOR ONE MINUTE.

Q: Who pays tithe on the high pasture?
A: The silence atop Psiloritis. Nobody's climbed up there. Its tribute comes down each August under wax.
Q: Whose seal?
A: My father's. We buried him with the ring.
p. 77: for "no one used Ravenna's bricked gate" read "1,306 came in." None left. The bricks are intact. Cf. the loft at the Hill Enclosure.

dice.callback: The loft at the Hill Enclosure

text: PUBLIC NOTICE. Will the silk works at Ushuaia, which has shipped 1,140 lb of raw silk to Liverpool yearly since 1885, kindly state where it is. No mulberry grows on the island and no one has found the works. Liverpool reports the silk is excellent and arrives cold.
Tr. note: the 1923 Berlin trade treaty is signed by one Ludwig Kemper, born 1958. The original verb is "will sign"; I gave "signed." The tense held, so he did. He has written asking for his pen back.

Polar MS 1053/7. Mess book, Cape Evans, winter 1911. Scope: an officer's tally of every joke told at dinner and the laughter it earned. On 9 June he entered the laughter first. Fourteen men laughed at nothing for 34 minutes, until he ruled a line beneath it.
hail-post, n. From Semipalatinsk, 1934, where hail fell upward all summer. The post office took letters to go up with it. None came back.

Kerasous, Absence of (1367). For seven days the Pontic town of Kerasous did not exist. Petitioners queued at its gate throughout and were heard. The judgments issued that week stand, and are enforced in Kerasous.

IN 1343 THE APOSTOLIC CAMERA TAXED SPRING AT ONE FLORIN A GARDEN. THIS STREET REFUSED, AND ITS SPRING WAS SEIZED AND LOCKED IN THE PALACE CELLARS. TULIPS BLOOM DOWN THERE EACH APRIL. UP HERE IT HAS BEEN MARCH SINCE.

Lot 219. Pepper casket, Ayutthaya, c. 1681, ex-Phra Khlang stores. Est. 900–1,200 ticals. Opening it causes a sneeze, a reflex withdrawn from mankind in 1702. Our cataloguer has sneezed and cannot describe it.
Tlatelolco market council, 1519. Motion to retire the market's hour of silence. Carried. The dead, who shopped in it, now shop with us.

CORRECTION. The Edo pawnbroker Ōmiya Seibei, whose death we printed on the 9th, never lived. There was no house, no birth, no face. His loans are being called in all the same, and every borrower remembers the money.

Kilwa Kisiwani, 1527.
2 Shawwal: unattended puppets perform in the market, their strings rising into a clear sky.
3 Shawwal: they pay the gate toll in Sofala gold, correctly weighed.
6 Shawwal: the qadi orders the strings cut. No puppet falls. Eleven townsmen do.
Sloop Anna Kristina, off Nólsoy, 4 May 1761. Paid the sea its toll, 3 rigsdaler. The change came up in the nets, one skilling short again. The sea prices a man at a skilling. Crew: 9 of 10.
Yokohama, 1873: From the Bluff, Fuji is visible only to those who speak English. Our cook pays an interpreter to describe it.
THE KLONDIKE RUSH BEGAN ON THIS CREEK WITH A BIRTHDAY WISH. A COOK'S GIRL OF SEVEN ASKED FOR GOLD IN THE WATER, AND THERE WAS. SHE IS BILLED ROYALTY ON EVERY OUNCE. SHE IS STILL SEVEN.

leap-hewer, n. A miner who exists only on 29 February. From the Iglau wage rolls, where the hewer Ondřej Malý is paid one day's wage every fourth year from 1404 onward. The mine master attests him diligent, sober, and, by 1496, twenty-four days older.
Eanna, Uruk. Barley, 30. Toll on the Euphrates, which left its bed in the drought to cross our fields one night: 2 sheep. The river paid.
LOST, Zante, 1810: the hum of Dionisio Kalos's hives. The bees work on in silence. The hum is now in the harbour clerk, who buzzes when he speaks and has billed Kalos for its board.
